'''Grażyna Jolanta Ciemniak''' (born 20 June 1948) is a Polish political figure who has been a member of the [[Senate of the Republic of Poland|Senate of Poland]] (1993–97) and [[List of presidents of Bydgoszcz|Deputy President of Bydgoszcz]] (1998–2001), as well as member of the [[Sejm of the Republic of Poland|Sejm of Poland]] (2001–07, since 2009) and [[member of the European Parliament]] (2004).

A native of the northern city of [[Toruń]], the co-capital and assembly location of the [[Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship]], Grażyna Ciemniak initially gained her Senate seat in the [[1993 Polish parliamentary election|1993 parliamentary election]]. While not in the Sejm during its 1997–2001 term, she served, in 1998–2001, as [[List of presidents of Bydgoszcz|Deputy President of Bydgoszcz]], a position subject to election by the [[Bydgoszcz City Council]].

In [[2001 Polish parliamentary election]], she campaigned for the Sejm IV term from [[Bydgoszcz's parliamentary district|Bydgoszcz district 4]] as candidate from the [[Democratic Left Alliance-Labor Union]] (SLD-UP) list<ref>[http://www.pkw.gov.pl/wybory/2001//040000/SSSS04/sjw1_k7o.html www.pkw.gov.pl] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716135127/http://www.pkw.gov.pl/wybory/2001//040000/SSSS04/sjw1_k7o.html |date=2011-07-16 }}. Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref> and was elected with 8,212 votes.<ref>[http://orka.sejm.gov.pl/ArchAll2.nsf/Glowny4kad www.orka.sejm.gov.pl] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191015145553/http://orka.sejm.gov.pl/ArchAll2.nsf/Glowny4kad |date=2019-10-15 }}. Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref> Between April 2003 (signed of [[Treaty of Accession 2003]]) and 31 April 2004, Grażyna Ciemniak was an [[Member of the European Parliament#Observers|observer]] representing the Sejm in the [[European Parliament]].<ref>[http://libr.sejm.gov.pl/oide/index.php?topic=international&id=obserwatorzy_pe libr.Sejm.gov.pl] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110820010645/http://libr.sejm.gov.pl/oide/index.php?topic=international&id=obserwatorzy_pe |date=2011-08-20 }}. Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref> Between 1 May and 19 July she served as a non-elected member of European Parliament V.<ref>[http://www.europarl.europa.eu/members/archive/alphaOrder/view.do?language=EN&id=23759 europarl.europa.eu]. Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref>

In [[2004 European Parliament election in Poland|2004 European Parliament election]] she was a candidate of [[Democratic Left Alliance-Labor Union]] from [[Kuyavian-Pomeranian (European Parliament constituency)|Kuyavian-Pomeranian constituency]]. She polled an insufficient 9,001 votes<ref>[http://isip.sejm.gov.pl/servlet/Search?todo=file&id=WDU20041371460&type=2&name=D20041460.pdf Dz.U. 2004 nr 137 poz. 1460]{{dead link|date=October 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. Page 12. Accessdate on 2009-05-21.</ref> and was not elected.

In [[2005 Polish parliamentary election|2005 parliamentary election]] she was started to the Sejm V Term from [[Bydgoszcz's parliamentary district|4 Bydgoszcz district]]. She polled 3,807 votes and was second on the [[Democratic Left Alliance (Poland)|Democratic Left Alliance]] (SLD) list<ref>[http://www.wybory2005.pkw.gov.pl/SJM/PL/WYN/W9/4.htm www.wybory2005.pkw.gov.pl] Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref> for the Sejm term which ended in 2007.

In [[2007 Polish parliamentary election|2007 parliamentary election]] she campaigned from a [[Left and Democrats]] (LiD) list for a chance to serve in Sejm VI, but polled only 3,997 votes and was the first LiD candidate to lose her seat.<ref>[http://wybory2007.pkw.gov.pl/SJM/PL/WYN/W7/4.htm www.wybory2007.pkw.gov.pl]. Accessdate on 2009-04-21.</ref> In June 2009, following [[Janusz Zemke]]'s win in his bid for a [[2009 European Parliament election in Poland|seat in the European Parliament]], she succeeded to his seat in the Sejm. She has been a [[List of Sejm members (2007–2011)|member of Sejm VI Term]] since 24 June 2009 as [[Social Democracy of Poland]] parliamentary club member.

Grażyna Ciemniak's son, {{Ill|Robert Ciemniak|lt=Robert|pl}} (born 1975), is a [[chess prodigy]] who has held the title of [[International Master]] since 1993.
